title: Board effect
description:
WHAT THIS PUTS ON THE MAP, in numbers a program can act on. Everything else about a trick or a feature is prose written for a person; this block is written for the board. Nothing here decides an outcome — it says where the thing goes and how big it is, works out who is inside it, and hands that list to the DM, who rolls and says what happened. See docs/MAP-INTERACTION.md.

It exists because the prose cannot be read by a program. `range` is free text ('30 feet', 'Self'), the area is a sentence ('a 10-foot radius centered on a point you choose within range'), and recovering a shape from that by pattern-matching got three of sixteen tricks wrong on the first attempt — it called an after-image that explicitly occupies no space a spawn, and a burst around a dead Clone a spawn as well. So the shape is authored, not inferred.

OMIT IT unless the trick actually puts something on the board. A trick that targets one creature you can see needs no board block: the target is already a figure on the map and the range is already in the prose. This is for areas, for figures that appear, and for figures that are moved.

DISTANCES ARE FEET, always, and multiples of 5 — the grid is 5 feet a square, and a 12-foot radius is not a thing anyone can draw on it.

verb.description:
The six things anything in this system does to the board, and there are only six.
  shape — an area is placed: a burst, a cloud, an illusion. Needs `shape` and `size`.
  spawn — a figure appears that somebody then controls. Needs `figure`.
  move  — a figure is put somewhere else: dragged, thrown, hauled. Needs `distance`.
  swap  — two figures exchange squares in ONE gesture: you and one of your own Clones. Not a move with a destination — the destination IS where the other one is standing, so there is nothing to aim and no distance to measure. `range` is how far away it may be.
  mark  — ground is marked and stays marked: a wall run, a line held. Needs `shape` and `size`.
  lock  — a figure stops moving. Where a condition already says so (restrained, grappled), the condition does the work and this only says the board should show it.

range.description: How far from the caster the thing may be placed, in feet. 0 means it happens where the caster is. This is DRAWN, never enforced — the reach shows as a ring and turns red outside it, exactly as movement does (RULES.md, and docs/MAP-INTERACTION.md 'Decided 2026-08-10').

anchor.description:
What the effect is centred on, which is not the same question as who it hurts.
  point    — anywhere within range; the caster picks the spot.
  self     — on the caster.
  creature — on a chosen figure.
  ally     — on a chosen friendly figure.
  clone    — on a figure the caster owns (a Clone, a spawned hand): the app knows where those are, so it does not have to ask.

shape.description: shape/mark only. `radius` is a circle on the grid (a sphere read from above); `cube` is a square of `size` on a side; `line` and `wall` also take a `width`.

size.description: shape/mark only, in feet: the radius of a radius, the edge of a cube, the length of a line, cone or wall.

width.description: line and wall only: how thick it is, in feet.

rounds.description: How many rounds the thing stays on the board. It ticks down with the order bar and clears itself at zero, for everyone, and the DM can clear it early. OMIT for something instantaneous — a burst that goes off, is resolved and is gone leaves nothing to draw. Ten rounds is a minute.

figure.description: spawn only: what appears, in a word or two — 'clone', 'puppet hand'. It becomes the figure's name on the board.

controlledBy.description: spawn only. A figure the caster controls acts INSIDE its owner's turn — it gets no slot of its own in the order and one 'Done' ends all of it (docs/MAP-INTERACTION.md, decided 2026-08-10).

distance.description:
move only: how far the figure goes, in feet. For a swap or a teleport this is the furthest the destination may be from where it started.

'speed' and 'half-speed' are for the moves measured against the figure's OWN speed rather than a fixed number — a Wall-Run is half your speed, and Grand Marionette moves someone else up to theirs. The board already knows every figure's speed, so it can draw those too.

aura.description: shape only: the area is fixed to whatever it is anchored to and travels with it — a ring around a figure rather than a patch of ground — and it lasts as long as the thing that made it does, which is why it carries no `rounds`. Guardian's Wall is the case: 10 feet around the Bulwark, wherever the Bulwark walks.

targets.description: move only: whether one figure moves or several chosen ones do.

mark.description: lock only: WHICH condition the board shows on the figure. Defaults to `grappled`, which is what a grapple is. A Puppeteer's String is the other case — Kayki, 2026-08-14: "a pupetteer dont have anyway to keep track on which creatures he has strings on… that creature gets an notify on top of it, like if its grappled or restrained, but instead, its with a string, that way we can all track it." It has to be a condition the whole table already reads, or it is a private note again: the figure shows it, the DM can clear it, and a second press of the same button takes it off, which is what "detach, no action" means.

label.description: What the button on the sheet says. Omit and the verb picks the words — 'Hold a figure', 'Move a figure', 'Trade places'. Worth setting the moment the verb's default is a lie: a String is not a grapple, and 'Hold a figure' would be the wrong instruction for it.

rangeAtLevel.description: A range that GROWS. `range` is the number at 1st level; each key here is the level from which the value applies, and the highest key at or below the character's level wins. Authored rather than computed because a formula mini-language for one or two cases is a language nobody else will ever read — Web of Strings taking a Puppeteer's leash from 60 feet to 90 at 5th is the case it exists for.

cap.description: lock only: how many of these may be attached at once. `engine` means the class's own engine cap is the answer — a Puppeteer may hold as many Strings as their String cap, and attaching one past it detaches the OLDEST, which is what the class says happens. The sheet is the only side that knows the cap, so it hands it to the board.

then.description: An area with no shape and no size is not an area.
Something appears; the board has to have something to call it.
A move with no distance cannot be drawn or measured.
A line has to be some number of feet thick to cover any squares at all.
